_comment: The pack this graph is built for: github.com/ostris/ComfyUI-Krea2-Ostris-Edit,
which krea2_style_reference and the openpose LoRA were trained against.
Different geometry from pack A, which is why it is a different file
and why the LoRA — not a mode switch — chooses between them. Here the
references are appended to the image token sequence and conditioned
at timestep 0 ('index_timestep_zero'), and Qwen3-VL sees them at a
deliberately coarse 384x384 total pixels. Feeding a pack A LoRA this
graph is out of distribution, not merely suboptimal.
The VAE is wired into the TEXT ENCODE node, which is where this pack
attaches the reference latents to the conditioning; the patch node
then consumes them off the conditioning rather than from a socket.
That patch node is a no-op when no reference latents are present.
kv_cache stays false: it is only correct for LoRAs trained with
ai-toolkit's kv_cache kwarg, and none of the ones we ship were.
Nodes 12/13 are the optional 2nd and 3rd references; unused slots are
dropped from the graph before submission.

2._note: The edit LoRA is not optional here the way a style LoRA is in the t2i graph: it IS the recipe. Without it the patched forward feeds source tokens to a model never trained to read them.

3._note: fp8_scaled conditioner, via ComfyUI's own CLIPLoader. Used only when the GGUF pair is absent: it costs ~700 s per request on gfx1201. It carries the Qwen3-VL vision weights natively, which image grounding requires.

5._note: Positive. The VAE connection is what turns the reference images into reference latents on the conditioning.

6._note: Negative: text-only, no images and no VAE — per the pack's own reference wiring. Unused at cfg 1.0.

7._note: EmptySD3LatentImage, not EmptyLatentImage: Krea 2's VAE is 16-channel and this latent is read by the patch node for the target geometry, not only by the sampler (which would have fixed the channel count itself).
